claims.statement: Let N=D^4, X in Z^(N x D), Y in Z^(D x N), and all entries have absolute value below 2^b. If W is supplied as a list of q rectangles (R_t,C_t) with explicit index sets, each side at least D, total multiplicity-counted area M=sum_t |R_t||C_t| <= N^(179/100), together with an explicit residual F outside their union of size at most N^(7/4-sigma) for fixed sigma>0, then all distinct requested dot products can be returned exactly with Q=O(ND + M D^(log_2(7)-2) + |F|D + M + |F|) integer scalar additions/subtractions/multiplications plus sorting/deduplication. The fixed seven-term 2x2 kernel has coefficient field Q, field degree 1, coefficient alphabet {−1,0,1}, and no algebraic setup search. For b=O(log N), including input-list reads and output materialization, the cost is O(N^(2-min{3/400,sigma}) polylog N).
assumptions: The supplied rectangles and residual list represent exactly the requested mask; F is outside the rectangle union.
The rectangle sets and residual entries are presented as explicit index lists; discovering such a representation is outside the algorithm interface.
Inputs are exact integers; the displayed subquadratic bit specialization assumes b=O(log N).
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact theorem; base identity exhaustively checked over Z
claims.novelty_boundary: Strassen's seven-product kernel is classical. The rectangle tiling corollary is elementary and priority is unknown. This result is a constructive narrow replacement for the non-materialized 9/4 kernel in the earlier conditional mask theorem; it does not cover arbitrary masks or the earlier N^(15/8) rectangle-volume endpoint.

costs.coefficient_heights: Only 0 and ±1; logarithmic height 0 for nonzero coefficients; 36 nonzero entries in 84 table slots.
costs.kernel_setup: Hard-coded table O(1); no search. Exhaustive exact verification is at most 448 sign-products, 384 additions, and 64 comparisons.
costs.compile_procedure: Uniform recursive interpreter uses O(1) source, O(log D) recursion depth, and O(Q) control steps; a fully unrolled gate listing has O(Q) gate records and O(Q log N) serialization bits.
costs.bit_cost: For general b, end-to-end O(Q(b+log N)^2 + (M+|F|)log(M+|F|)(b+log N)), including matrix and mask reads, output writing, and sorting; for b=O(log N), O(N^(2-min{3/400,sigma}) polylog N).
costs.mask_representation: O((M/D+|F|)log N) bits from explicit index lists; no cost bound for discovering the cover from an arbitrary mask.
costs.output: At most M+|F| distinct exact values, each with at most 2b+ceil(log_2 D)+O(1) bits.

claims.falsifier: An error in any of the 64 checked tensor coordinates, the exact Strassen recurrence counts, the tile-count inequality, padding correctness, or the O(b+log N) intermediate-height bound invalidates the theorem. The script tests the base identity exhaustively but only tests recursive/selective execution on finite fixtures.
claims.next_gate: Independent mathematical review of the bit-growth and representation accounting; preserve the claim as a structured-mask result unless a separately proved mechanism yields covers for a broader mask class.

claims.statement: The pinned page-9 proof derives an existential fixed base size u and exact rank-r decomposition from the asymptotic exponent definition but supplies no effective u, r, number-field degree, coefficient-height bound, or search stopping-time bound. The claim that a complex solution implies a rational solution is invalid generally; a point over Qbar suffices to put each witness in some finite number field but gives no explicit resource bounds.
assumptions: Pinned source is the OpenAI math release commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a.
Source page 9 is read directly; no assumption that the exponent theorem itself is false.
